title: Coefficient/exponent pair (1, 1) for the fixed OR family, proved self-contained

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total OR family defined in proof.md: f_0=0 on the empty input; for n>=1, f_n(x)=1 iff at least one input bit x_i is 1. One fixed polynomial-time evaluator scans the input once. The same family is used at every length.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one total uniform polynomial-time family, hence in NP with empty witnesses, C_B2(f_n)=n-1 for every n>=2, hence C_B2(f_n)>=(1)*n-o(n); in particular liminf C_B2(f_n)/n>=1 at every sufficiently large integer length n=|x| in the full Li-Yang B2 model.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: C_B2(f_n) = n-1 for every integer n >= 2 for the OR family of proof.md (exact equality: the n-1-gate binary OR tree upper bound and the connectivity lower bound).

LP arithmetic lemma (unscored): at alpha_I=48/5, alpha_Q=9/5, alpha_phi=1/5, delta=64/5, the six Li-Yang Theorem 4.1 expressions equal 16/5, 17/5, 16/5, 16/5, 16/5, 16/5, and weighting rows 4, 5, 6 by 7/10, 1/10, 1/5 gives u <= 31/10 + alpha_phi/2. This is pure rational arithmetic only and establishes no circuit bound by itself.
